title: An ex-U.S. Labor Secretary and a Gen Z historian talk politics, protest and capitalism
summary: CNBC assembled notable voices from different generations to discuss success and happiness in America's 250th anniversary year. Former Labor Secretary Robert Reich (80) conversed with Gen Z historian Kahlil Greene (26) to explore intergenerational perspectives on politics, protest, and capitalism.
content: To recognize the country’s 250th year, CNBC Make It got notable voices in politics, finance and relationships across age ranges to sit down and spark conversation about what it means to achieve happiness and success in this country today. Robert Reich, 80, a former Secretary of Labor during Bill Clinton's administration, spoke with Kahlil Greene, 26, a history newsletter writer and content creator.

zh.title: 美国前劳工部长与Z世代历史学家讨论政治、抗争和资本主义
zh.summary: CNBC汇集了来自不同代际的杰出人物，讨论美国建国250周年之际的成功与幸福。80岁的美国前劳工部长罗伯特·赖希与26岁的Z世代历史学家卡利尔·格林进行了对话，探讨了跨代视角下关于政治、抗争和资本主义的观点。

title: How to plan for the high cost of having your first kid in your 40s
summary: As delayed parenthood becomes more common, older first-time parents face significant financial planning challenges. The article explores strategies for managing elevated costs of having children later in life.
content: Older parenthood is on the rise — but it comes with a tough new set of financial rules.

zh.title: 如何规划40多岁生育第一个孩子的高成本
zh.summary: 随着延迟生育变得越来越普遍，年长的初次父母面临重大的财务规划挑战。该文章探讨了应对晚年生育成本升高的策略。

title: Faisal Islam: Four reasons why Fifa's World Cup plan never stacked up
summary: FIFA's proposal to part-privatize the World Cup faces fundamental structural challenges according to analysis. The plan's presentation raised more unresolved questions than solutions, casting doubt on its viability.
content: The actual presentation of FIFA's plan to part-privatise the World Cup raises many more questions than it answers.

title: Spain installs floating barrier in North African enclave following border rush by tens of thousands
summary: Spain deployed a floating barrier in the North African enclave of Ceuta following an unprecedented surge of approximately 50,000 border crossings. The mass movement occurred through both land and sea routes.
content: According to Spanish authorities, about 50,000 people crossed into Ceuta by land and sea from Thursday in an unprecedented surge.

title: As Americans go direct with GLP-1 prescriptions, Walmart, Costco, Amazon will be big weight-loss winners
summary: Retail giants Walmart, Costco, and Amazon are positioned to benefit significantly from the trend of Americans obtaining GLP-1 weight-loss drugs directly through prescriptions. The direct-prescription model creates new market-capture opportunities for large pharmacy chains.
content: As Americans are encouraged to go direct with weight-loss drug prescriptions, retail pharmacy chains are poised to win big.

title: From a Fed decision to Big Tech earnings: What drove last week's volatile market

title: Wildfires rage in Greece as firefighters continue battle in France and Spain
summary: Wildfires are spreading across Southern Europe with ongoing battles in Greece, France, and Spain. Record-low water levels on the Danube have simultaneously reduced nuclear and hydroelectric power production in Hungary and Serbia.
content: Production of nuclear power in Hungary and hydropower in Serbia has fallen because of record low water levels along the Danube.

title: OpenAI's Hugging Face hack confirmed months of AI cyber warnings: 'Pandora's box is open'
summary: A security breach affecting OpenAI and Hugging Face has validated months of industry warnings about AI system vulnerabilities. The incident, discussed at the Black Hat cybersecurity conference, underscores escalating risks in the AI sector.

title: To keep growing, incoming Best Buy CEO says he first wants to go smaller
summary: Incoming Best Buy CEO Jason Bonfig plans to downsize operations as a strategic approach to future growth. His focus is on expanding market reach and improving the customer experience through a more targeted footprint.

title: Is the government lying to us about inflation?
summary: Questions have emerged regarding the accuracy of government inflation measurements through the consumer-price index. These figures are critical as they determine Social Security adjustments and returns on inflation-protected Treasury securities.
content: The concern is understandable, since the consumer-price index affects everything from Social Security’s annual cost-of-living adjustment to the interest rate earned by investors in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities.

title: Stick to spending limits, PM and chancellor tell ministers in joint memo
summary: The UK Chancellor and Prime Minister jointly instructed government ministers to adhere to spending limits ahead of the October 28 Budget. The guidance emphasizes that the Budget will "meet our fiscal rules" and provide economic stability for households planning ahead.
content: The Chancellor said the Budget on 28 October would “meet our fiscal rules” and give families "stability" to plan for the future.

title: Building for 131°F: Europe races to protect its infrastructure from a ‘quiet catastrophe’

content: A summer of weather extremes and severe infrastructure stress has prompted companies and policymakers across Europe to respond.

title: Iran's overlapping power centers make ending the war more complicated

title: My ex-husband’s sister died — so why is Fidelity asking me for her death certificate?

title: Soccer-FIFA scraps World Cup sell-off plan after resistance from members
